question.text: The point $Q$ with coordinates $(-1, 1)$ lies on the curve $y = f(x)$ and the point $R$ with coordinates $(-1, -2)$ lies on the curve $y = g(x).$ If the curve $y = g(x)$ is related to $y = f(x)$ via the transformation $g(x) = f(x) + k$, then what is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
First, notice that the point $R(-1, -2)$ lies $3$ units below the point $Q(-1, 1).$ So, the graph of $y = g(x)$ can be obtained from the graph of $y = f(x)$ by shifting it $3$ units down.

As a result, $k = -3.$

example.title: Identifying the Vertical Shift of a Translated Function

question.text: The point $P$ with coordinates $(2, -1)$ lies on the curve $y = f(x) - 3.$ Which of the following points must lie on $y = f(x) + 1?$
question.explanation:
Method 1

The graph of $y = f(x)+1$ is obtained by translating the graph of $y=f(x)-3$ by $4$ units up.

Hence, if the point $(2,-1)$ lies on $y=f(x)-3$, then the point \[ (2,-1+4) = (2,3) \] lies on $y=f(x) + 1.$

Method 2

As $(2,-1)$ lies on $y = f(x) - 3$, we have:

\begin{align*} f(2) - 3 &= -1 \\[3pt] f(2) &= -1 + 3 \\[3pt] f(2) &= 2 \end{align*}

Now, if $x = 2$ then

\begin{align*} y &= f(2) + 1\\ &= 2 + 1\\ &= 3. \end{align*}

So, the point $(2, 3)$ must lie on $y = f(x) + 1.$

example.title: Identifying Points that Must Lie on a Translated Curve

question.text: The point $Q$ with coordinates $(-2, 1)$ lies on the curve $y = f(x)$ and the point $R$ with coordinates $(-2, -1)$ lies on the curve $y = g(x).$ If the curve $y = g(x)$ is related to $y = f(x)$ via the transformation $g(x) = f(x) + k$, then what is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
First, notice that the point $R(-2, -1)$ lies $2$ units below the point $Q(-2, 1).$ So, the graph of $y = g(x)$ can be obtained from the graph of $y = f(x)$ by shifting it $2$ units down.

As a result, $k = -2.$
